speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand the nature of your symptoms better. Does your double vision occur in one eye or does it disappear if you close one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular issue. Given your double vision specifically worsens with upward or downward gaze, do you notice any difficulty with swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Antibodies_for_Myasthenia_Gravis (AChR, MuSK). REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CXR. Do you experience any eyelid drooping or changes in the clarity of your vision when you look down after standing for a while?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Chest_CXR: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected; Ptosis: Yes (drooping of the right upper eyelid worsening with upward gaze); Diplopia: Yes (worsens with looking up or down); Fatigability: Yes (weakness worsens after activity, improves with rest).
